decision: Which page format tells the What's included story best: the order of a family's month, with every product shown and interactive?
primary_axis: page structure (how the chapters are laid out and connected)
invariants: Same chapters and copy: assessment, workbook, the stuck beat (Day 4, page 2, question 11: 300 - 128), AI Teaching Assistant, Unica app, dashboard, next workbook, month at a glance, closing cards, pricing, FAQ
Same product screens from Figma; Leah throughout; level switch Leah U10 / Mateo U19 (D-173)
Warm look tokens: white page, Geist and Geist Mono, orange square, grainy colour fields, 6 px controls
Closing recap in the Superpower card layout in every option (Savar, 2026-10-29)

options.name: A month with Leah
options.bet: Chronology by date and time: each chapter is a moment in Leah's month, a real photo with the real product screen on it, alternating sides, with a dated chapter map
options.benefit: The most story-like and human; the dates make the order and the time cost obvious
options.cost: Needs a good photo for each moment; product screens are smaller because they sit on photos; the longest page
options.risk: Reads as lifestyle; parents may not see enough product detail without opening each part

options.name: One stage
options.bet: One fixed stage while the page scrolls: the step list on the left advances, and the object on the right changes from report to workbook to laptop to phone to laptop to workbook
options.benefit: The shortest page; the six products read as one connected system in one place
options.cost: Scroll-driven stage is the most work to build and test; phones need a separate stacked layout
options.risk: Scroll control can feel heavy, and each product gets less room to be explored inside the stage

options.name: Chapters to explore
options.bet: Each product is its own chapter with a large product view on a colour field and a row of tabs to explore it; handwritten notes point at parts; one dark band; a pill menu that stays at the top
options.benefit: The most product depth and one interaction pattern (tabs) for every product; easy deep links for outreach
options.cost: Less emotional; the story order depends on the pill menu and the numbering
options.risk: Can read as a feature catalogue and lose the one-child story

outcome: Savar, 2026-10-29: none picked. Kept: header A and the closing card recap. Rejected: the dated chapter map pills (confusing), dates and step numbers on chapters, stock photos and small product screens. Next round r159.
